task: Write a due diligence memo on Deel

merged.claim: Alex Bouaziz is Deel co-founder and CEO; Shuo Wang is co-founder and Chief Revenue Officer.
Joe Kauffman was appointed Deel President and CFO on 2025-11-03. He is a former Credit Karma CFO, President and CEO, and an Intuit executive. C reads the appointment as signalling IPO intent.
Dan Westgarth is Deel COO. He was previously in senior roles at Revolut and leads global operations.
Philippe Bouaziz is Deel Executive Chairman and Chief Strategy Officer. He is the father of the CEO, a former Deel CFO and a founder partner, and founded Prodware Group.

Other Deel executives are Yaron Lavi (CTO, ex-VP R&D at Zira and Amdocs), Harish Sharma (Chief Risk Officer), DeAnn Work (Global Corporate General Counsel) and Anthony Rodriguez (Chief Compliance Officer). Deel built out its compliance bench in 2025.
Harish Sharma joined as Chief Risk Officer in July 2025 from Pagaya, with prior risk roles at Bank of America and HSBC North America.
Co-founder Ofer Simon is listed on Wikipedia as a 2019 Deel co-founder but is absent from Deel's current leadership page, with no documented departure.
CEO Alex Bouaziz told Fortune (Nov 2025) that 80% of his leadership team is unchanged since $0 ARR. The article says the workforce grew from 10 to 3,600.
Deel was founded in 2019 by Alex Bouaziz, Shuo Wang and Ofer Simon through Y Combinator. Bouaziz was 25 at launch, and he and Wang met at MIT in 2013.
Founder backgrounds: Bouaziz previously co-founded Sarona Ventures and studied at Technion and MIT. Wang co-founded Aeris Cleantec and was its CTO until its acquisition by iRobot.
Communications chief Elisabeth Diana (ex-Instagram/Facebook) left Deel in April 2025, confirmed by Deel, amid the Rippling lawsuit. Causation is not established.
Company claim: Shuo Wang led Deel from $1M to $100M ARR in under 20 months.
Deel Series A (May 2020) was $14M led by Andreessen Horowitz.
AccessIPOs lists the 2020 Series A as $18.61M at a $63M valuation.
Deel Series B (Sept 2020) was $30M led by Spark Capital, with Y Combinator and angels, at ~$230M valuation. Total funding then exceeded $48M, which may explain Wikipedia's $48M figure.
Deel Series C (April 2021) was $156M, making Deel a unicorn at ~$1.25B valuation (range cited ~$1.14-1.3B). A says it was led by YC Continuity; C cites a16z participation.

Deel Series D (Oct 2021) was $425M led by Coatue (with DST Global per C) at a $5.5B valuation. Participants included Altimeter, a16z, Neo, Spark and YC Continuity, and cumulative funding exceeded $630M.
Deel raised ~$50M in May 2022 at a $12B valuation, led by Emerson Collective. This is press-reported (Axios/TechCrunch) and not confirmed by a filing. The CEO disclosed a $100M ARR rate at the time.
In February 2025 Deel was valued at $12.6B after a ~$300M secondary purchase by General Catalyst and Mubadala (Abu Dhabi). This was secondary liquidity, not primary capital.
Deel says General Catalyst and a sovereign investor bought close to $300M of secondary shares from early investors in April 2025.

Deel Series E (announced 2025-10-20) was $300M at a $17.3B valuation, co-led by new investor Ribbit Capital with Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue. It is the latest verified priced round. Proceeds are earmarked for acquisitions.
Company claim: Deel has raised more than $1B in total funding.
Deel's owned global payroll engine is live in 55+ countries, with a goal of native payroll in 100+ countries by 2029.
The CEO said in Feb 2025 that Deel was preparing for an IPO as soon as 2026 (CNBC). In June 2025 he said it still targets a 2026 US IPO, dependent on macro conditions. No S-1 is public.

Deel is a Delaware-incorporated, San Francisco-based, remote-first global HR/payroll/EOR platform. It covers EOR, contractors, immigration, HRIS, benefits, mobility and IT, and targets startups through enterprise.
Company claim: Deel operates in 150+ countries with EOR in 130+ countries, owns ~250 legal entities, and holds financial licenses in the US, Canada, UK and EU.
Deel pricing as of 2026-10-21: contractor management from $49/contractor/month, Contractor of Record $325/month, US PEO $125/employee/month, EOR $599/employee/month.
Competitors named include Rippling, Omnipresent and ADP.
Company claim: Deel serves 35,000+ customers and 1.5M+ workers in 150+ countries and processes ~$22B in annual payroll (June 2025: 35,000 customers and 1.25M workers). Payroll volume is not revenue.
Company claim: Deel has 40,000+ customers (as of 2026-10-13).

Named customers include Reddit, Klarna, Cloudflare, ElevenLabs, Nike, Shopify, Anthropic, Intuit, Uber, Coinbase and Citi. Case studies include Revolut, FICO, Puma, Outreach and Zip Co. In 2021 customers included Coinbase, Dropbox and Shopify.
Deel's customer count grew from ~1,800 (April 2021) to 4,500+ (October 2021) per TechCrunch.
Company claim: since early 2024, customers using 3+ products rose 480% and those using 4+ products rose 1,200%.
Company claim: since early 2024 Deel's HR suite grew 600%, US payroll/PEO adoption 1,500%, Mobility 220%, IT 410% and global payroll 450%.
Deel is a certified Workday Global Payroll Cloud partner with expanded SAP, UKG and NetSuite integrations. Barings uses Deel with Workday across 18 countries (March 2026).
Deel became Arsenal F.C.'s HR partner in a multi-year deal announced 2025-12-12, and Arsenal is a platform customer. It became sleeve sponsor in May 2026.
Deel claimed a $1B annual revenue run rate in Q1 2025, with revenue up 75% for the 12 months to April 30, 2025 (management statements, unaudited).
Deel reported a 16% EBITDA margin in Q1 2025.
Deel earmarked a $200-500M M&A budget for 2025 (up to $500M per Reuters).
Deel's first $100M revenue month was September 2025, with EBITDA of ~$15-17M per the CEO (Reuters). The company says it has been profitable for three years, on an unspecified basis.
Company-reported ARR trajectory: $4M (2020), $54M (2021), $100M (2022), ~$500M (2024), $1B run rate Q1 2025.
Deel told Calcalist (Sept 2023) it had $295M ARR, up from $57M a year earlier.
Deel said in March 2024 it had over $500M ARR achieved organically (excluding PaySpace), 3,000 team members in 100+ countries and 1.5 years of EBITDA profitability.
Deel claimed in March 2025 an $800M run rate, a $12B+ valuation and 2.5 years of profitability.
Deel claims it exceeded $1.5B ARR in H1 2026 and continued profitable growth (company-defined, unaudited).
Aggregator ARR.club (unverified) estimates Deel ARR of $1.2B (Oct 2025), $1.4B (Mar 2026, 40K+ customers) and $1.5B (Aug 2026), a +19% annualized CAGR.

Red flag: Deel's ARR, EBITDA and profitability figures are company- or management-defined and unaudited, with no public S-1 or audited filings. Audited revenue, margins and cash flow are needed before relying on the $17.3B valuation.
Deel headcount was 3,000 in March 2024.
Deel had ~5,000 employees in February 2025.
Deel had 6,500+ team members across 100+ countries as of June 2025. C also attributes 6,500+ to March 2024, which conflicts with the 3,000 figure.
Company claim: Deel has 7,000+ team members in 110+ countries.
Deel headcount reached 7,500 in 2025; no layoffs were found.
Deel acquired PaySpace (South African native payroll) in March 2024, its second 2024 acquisition.
Deel acquired Safeguard Global's payroll division in March 2025 for an undisclosed amount.
Deel acquired London-based rival Omnipresent for around $15M (per a person familiar, Reuters, Oct 2025).
By end of 2025 Deel had acquired 13 companies, including Zeitgold, Roots, Paygroup, Legalpad, Capbase, Zavvy, PaySpace, Hofy, Atlantic Money, Assemble and Safeguard Global's payroll division.
Deel acquired AI identity-verification/deepfake-detection firm Clarity (Israel), announced 2026-08-04, as its 15th acquisition. Terms were undisclosed.
Deel was named to the CNBC Disruptor 50 (2024) and the top 10 of the Forbes Cloud 100 (2025).

Rippling sued Deel on 2025-03-17 in N.D. Cal. (People Center, Inc. v. Deel, 3:25-cv-02576-CRB). It alleges corporate espionage, trade-secret misappropriation, racketeering, tortious interference and unfair competition. These are allegations only; no liability finding.

Rippling's amended complaint (June 5, 2025) adds RICO claims. It accuses CEO Alex Bouaziz of orchestrating the plot via a 'Bouaziz Racketeering Enterprise' with his father Philippe Bouaziz, names Philippe Bouaziz and COO Westgarth as defendants, and alleges at least four other competitors were targeted.

Rippling employee Keith O'Brien (Dublin) swore an affidavit (April 2025) admitting ~4 months of searching Rippling's Slack and Google Drive for Deel for a €5,000 monthly retainer (later crypto). He was caught via a fake 'd-defectors' Slack honeypot. He says CEO Alex Bouaziz recruited him and payments were discussed with Philippe Bouaziz; the evidence is disputed.

Unsealed bank records (Calcalist, Nov 2025) show Deel's $6,000 payment to the confessed spy was routed through an account of the COO's wife and arrived 56 seconds later. Rippling asked what Deel disclosed to its auditors.
Deel admitted in court (June 2025) that it instructed 'discreet surveillance' on the manager at the center of the spy case, after its lawyer initially denied it.

Deel denies Rippling's allegations. It countersued Rippling on April 24, 2025 in Delaware Superior Court alleging Rippling espionage and anti-competitive conduct, and voluntarily dismissed that suit in 2026. Counterclaims are not a judgment.
On Aug 20, 2025 a court reportedly dismissed Rippling's RICO and fraud claims ('unified corporate structure, not a distinct RICO enterprise'); trade-secret claims survived.
On 2026-02-23 the court denied Deel's attempts to dismiss Rippling's RICO and federal trade-secret claims against Deel and executives (and refused transfer), dismissing certain state-law claims.
The Rippling v. Deel case remained active as of mid/late October 2026, with ongoing discovery, sealing motions and a discovery status conference set for Nov 5, 2026.
The DOJ reportedly opened a criminal investigation into Deel over the Rippling spy allegations (WSJ, Jan 23, 2026). Deel said it is 'not aware of any investigation' and would cooperate.
DOJ grand jury subpoenas were reportedly issued in January 2026 in N.D. Cal. as part of the Deel criminal probe.

Red flag: The Rippling litigation, with espionage allegations naming Deel and senior executives, is a material legal and reputational overhang. TechCrunch called it 'arguably the biggest drama between two HR startups ever'.

Surge receiver complaint (Damian v. Deel, S.D. Fla. 1:25-cv-20017, filed 2025-01-03) alleged unlicensed money transmission, AML/KYC/OFAC failures, Russia sanctions-evasion facilitation and RICO. Deel denied wrongdoing and called it 'deeply inaccurate', noting a co-filer was reportedly an early Rippling investor. Allegations only.
Damian v. Deel was dismissed and closed on 2025-08-18 for lack of Article III standing; allegations not adjudicated.
Damian v. Deel was dismissed on Aug 19, 2025.
TechStartups retracted its Jan 2025 article on the Deel Ponzi/laundering lawsuit after Deel disputed inaccuracies.

Deel facilitated $72M+ in payments (40,000+ transactions) for MyForexFunds, which the CFTC accused of a Ponzi scheme, serving 15,664 of its customers (Nov 2021-Oct 2022). Deel said this was under 1% of revenue and it froze the account once informed.

A Minnesota Commerce consent order dated 2024-05-23 concerns alleged unlicensed cash-advance/lending and money-transmission activity by Deel, as reproduced in the Surge complaint. Terms and penalty are unverified.
Deel's DPayments subsidiary held 26 state money-transmission licenses as of early 2025; there is no SEC wrongdoing accusation against Deel.
Former Deel workers claimed misclassification in March 2023, and Deel denied the allegations.
California Sen. Steve Padilla asked the state labor agency to investigate Deel over worker misclassification in June 2023. Disposition is unverified.
California Sen. Steve Padilla requested a labor-agency investigation of Deel on 2023-07-06, alleging misclassification of its own workers and problematic client advice. Disposition is unverified.

Glassdoor shows Deel at 4.3/5 from 2,132 reviews, with 83% recommending and 88% approving of the CEO. Compensation/benefits are 4.0/5, down 6% over 12 months. Reviews praise remote flexibility, autonomy and learning, and cite intense pace, burnout, compensation/progression and communication concerns.
Deel's homepage shows a 4.7/5 rating from 15,401 G2 reviews (company-published).
G2 shows Deel Payroll at 4.7/5 from 7,288 reviews. Positives are ease of use and fast payments; recurring negatives are high fees, delays and withdrawal issues.

Trustpilot shows Deel at 4.6/5 from 9,680 reviews. Praise covers usability, transfers and onboarding; complaints cover slow support, payout delays, conflicting withdrawal information and policy changes.
BBB shows 17 complaints against Deel over three years, with eight closed in the prior 12 months, concerning billing, payroll/funds access, withdrawals and support. These are unverified by BBB.
Red flag: Review aggregators show recurring complaints about support responsiveness, payout/withdrawal delays and fees, warranting customer-reference checks.

Company claim: Deel has secured more than $1 billion in total funding at a $17.3 billion valuation.
Company claim: Deel surpassed $1 billion ARR in 2025, recorded three consecutive years of profitability, and had its first $100 million revenue month in September 2025.
Reuters reported CEO Alex Bouaziz said September 2025 was Deel's first month above $100 million revenue and that EBITDA was roughly $15-17 million.
Company claim: Shuo Wang led Deel from $1 million to $100 million ARR in under 20 months.
Company claim: Deel has 7,000+ team members worldwide in 110+ countries.
Reuters reported Deel crossed a $1 billion annual revenue run rate in Q1 2025 and earmarked up to $500 million for acquisitions in 2025.
Rippling sued Deel in N.D. California in March 2025 alleging racketeering, trade-secret misappropriation, tortious interference, unfair competition and related claims (allegations, not adjudicated).

Reuters reported former Rippling employee Keith O'Brien said in an Irish-court affidavit that Deel CEO Alex Bouaziz recruited him to provide confidential information and that payments were discussed with Deel CFO Philippe Bouaziz; the evidence is disputed.
The Rippling v. Deel federal case remained active as of October 20, 2026, with ongoing discovery, sealing motions and a discovery status conference scheduled for November 5, 2026.
Deel denies Rippling's allegations and says it filed counterclaims alleging anti-competitive conduct and misinformation; counterclaims are not a court judgment.

Trustpilot shows Deel at 4.6/5 from 9,680 reviews, with praise for usability, transfers and onboarding but complaints about slow support, payout delays, conflicting withdrawal information and policy changes.
G2 shows Deel Payroll at 4.7/5 from 7,288 reviews, citing ease of use and fast payments as positives and high fees, delays and withdrawal issues as recurring negatives.
Red flag: The Rippling litigation, including corporate espionage allegations naming Deel and senior executives, is a material legal and reputational overhang with active discovery as of October 2026.
Red flag: Deel's key operating and profitability metrics (ARR, EBITDA, profitability) are company- or management-reported and not supported by public audited filings in the sources reviewed.
Red flag: Review aggregators show recurring complaints about Deel's support responsiveness, payout/withdrawal delays and fees, warranting customer-reference checks.
